text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

THOMAS CRANMER, the English cleric who was consecrated Archbishop of Canterbury for his support of HENRY VIII in obtaining a divorce, was born in 1489. Archbishop CRANMER'S good fortune came to an abrupt end during the reign of QUEEN MARY. He was burnt at the stake as a heretic.
German novelist, HERMAN HESSE, was born in 1877. He is best known for "Siddartha", "Steppenwolf" and "The Glass Bead Game."

West Australian journalist, MURIEL CHASE, was born in 1880. She was the 'Aunt Mary' who wrote "Children's Corner" and helped start the Silver Chain District Nurses. They cycled to visit their patients.
The South Australian bushman, BOB BUCK, was born in 1881. He found and buried the body of the explorer LASSITER - of Reef Fame.
US singer PAUL WILLIAMS, who was a founding member of the 'Temptations', was born in 1939.
UK bass player with the 'Groundhogs', PETER CRUICKSHANK, was born in 1945.
'Boomtown Rats' bass player, PETER BRIQUETTE, was born in 1954.
** EVENTS **
1566 : French astrologer, NOSTRADAMUS, died. His death on
this day was one of his accurate predictions.
1644 : The Battle of Marston Moor near York brought the
first major Royalist defeat in the English Civil War.
1778 : JEAN-JACQUES ROUSSEAU, Swiss-born French
philosopher, died insane. He introduced the concept of "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity".
1819 : The Factory Act was passed in Britain, prohibiting
employment of children under nine in textile factories, and children under 16 could only work for 12 hours a day.
1850 : Sir ROBERT PEEL, British prime minister (1834-46)
and founder of the police force, died as a result of a riding accident.
1853 : The Russian army crossed the Pruth River, invading
Turkey and beginning the Crimean War.
1865 : British evangelist, WILLIAM BOOTH, established a

mission along military lines. His "Salvation Army" acted as a social service and reforming organisation for the most destitute members of society. He founded the mission in Whitechapel, one of London's worst slums.
1881 : JAMES GARFIELD, 20th president of the United
States, was shot in Washington. He died in September.
1900 : Aviation history was made in Germany when Count

FERDINAND VON ZEPPELIN flew his first airship for an hour. It took ZEPPELIN three years to build his airship. The dirigible balloon over a rigid frame was the largest to be built, measuring 136 metres in length. On its maiden voyage the airship reached speeds of up to 32 km an hour. The Zeppelins were used to bomb England during World War I and served as luxury passenger aircraft, until they were abandoned after several disasters in the 1920s and 1930s.
1937 : American pilot AMELIA EARHART and navigator FRED
NOONAN took off from Lae, New Guinea, on their around the world flight. They failed to arrive at their next destination in the Central Pacific and their fate remains unknown to this day.
1951 : The worst floods in US history left 41 dead and
200,000 homeless in Kansas and Missouri.
1961 : ERNEST HEMINGWAY, U.S. novelist best known for "A
Farewell to Arms" and "For Whom the Bell Tolls", shot himself.
1964 : US President LYNDON B. JOHNSON signed the Civil
Rights Bill outlawing racial discrimination.
1969 : 'Rolling Stone' BRIAN JONES drowned in his
swimming pool at Hartfield in Essex.
1973 : Hollywood star and 1940s pin-up BETTY GRABLE died.
The bouncy blonde insured her legs, which were said to be her best feature, for 200,000 dollars. Her films included "Tin Pan Alley", "Moon Over Miami" and "Coney Island".
1976 : North and South Vietnam were reunited in the

aftermath of the fall of Saigon and the end of the Vietnam war. A peace treaty was signed between the north and south in 1973, the year the US withdrew. In March 1975, the North invaded the South and took Saigon. The Socialist Republic of Vietnam was officially proclaimed on this day.
1985 : The ill-fated "Australia Card" proposal was
outlined by Health Minister Dr BLEWETT. It was rejected by the ALP amid protests of invasion of privacy with the ID card.
1985 : Allan BORDER scored his 5,000th test run in
Australia's win over England in the second test.
1990 : 100 Muslim pilgrims died of suffocation in a
tunnel in the Holy City of Mecca.
1994 : Colombian soccer player ANDRES ESCOBAR was shot
and killed in Medellin, after he had scored an own-goal in a World Cup match against the United States that put his country out of the tournament.
1994 : An Albanian court sentenced former Communist
president RAMIZ ALIA to nine years jail for abuse of power and violation of citizens' rights.
